title.narrative: Pacific Resilience Project II under the Pacific Resilience Program

description.narrative: The Objective of the Project in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is to strengthen early warning systems, climate resilient investments in shoreline protection, and to provide immediate and effective response to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

The objective of the Second Phase of Pacific Resilience Projects in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is to strengthen early warning systems, climate resilient investments in shoreline protection, and to provide immediate and effective response to an eligible crisis or emergency. There are four components to the project, the first component being institutional strengthening, early warning and preparedness. Component one has two sub-components: (i) institutional strengthening, central agency capacity building in risk governance, early warning, and modernization of the NDMO's facilities (which will be implemented by RMI); and (ii) NDMO capacity building, and post disaster needs assessment (which will be implemented by the SPC). The second component is the strengthening coastal resilience. Component two is divided into two sub-components: (a) coastal vulnerability assessment and protection investments (which will be implemented by RMI); and (b) strengthening coastal risk planning (which will be implemented by SPC). The third component is the contingency emergency response. This government-led component will include carrying out a program of activities designed to provide rapid response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed. This Contingency Emergency Response Component (CERC) may be used following the declaration of a disaster event. The CERC will complement the PCRAFI disaster insurance mechanism financed under PREP Phase I and will strengthen the emergency preparedness and immediate response capacity of RMI for low- and medium-scale disasters or disasters that are not covered by the PCRAFI insurance scheme (e.g. flood, drought). Finally, the fourth component is the project and program management. Component 4 is divided into two sub-components: (1) project Management (which will be implemented by RMI); and (2) program management (which will be implemented by SPC).

condition.narrative: SCHEDULE 1 Section V: To ensure availability of adequate funds for the Project, RMI shall take all reasonable measures required ornecessary on its part to secure, by not later than January 1, 2019, an amount of at least twenty-five million Dollars(US$25,000,000) to assist in financing of the Project.

SCHEDULE 2 Section I C 1: RMI shall prepare, by no later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, and thereafter adopt amanual, that is in form and substance acceptable to the Association, setting forth the arrangements and procedures forimplementation of the Project, including: (a) institutional arrangements for day to day execution of the Project; (b) theprocurement plan and implementation arrangements; (c) implementation arrangements for Safeguard Instruments; (d) budgeting,disbursement, and financial management arrangements; (e) Project monitoring, reporting, and evaluation arrangements, includingperformance indicators; (f) performance indicators; and (g) criteria and procedures for identifying additional areas for activitiesunder Part 2 of the Project (“Project Operations Manual”).

The Recipient shall establish, by not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, throughout theProject implementation period, a National Steering Committee, with a mandate, adequate resources and composition satisfactory tothe Association, with further details described in said Section.

The Recipient shall maintain, throughout the Project implementation period, a PIU within MOF, with a mandate, adequate resourcesand composition satisfactory to the Association, which shall be responsible for, inter alia, carrying out day-to-day implementationof the Project, with support from specialists from other departments and/or units of MOF.

The Recipient shall, by not later than 4 months after the Effective Date, enter into and thereafter maintain, until the closingdate specified in the SPC PREP II Financing Agreement, a Service Agreement with SPC.

title.narrative: % of communication stations operating in line with Standard operating procedures (SOPs) in outer island network

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to Subcomponent 1.1.2 Early warning communication systems improvement. Building on the work done by IOM on Community Disaster Risk Management - Emergency Communications Training, NDMO and Outland Focal Points, critical requirements and gaps in outer islands are identified. The EC Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) were developed and tested. The NDMO focal points of the outer islands (identified as the communication stations), will conduct an annual test, during the ‘Outer Islands Focal Point Workshop’ organized by IOM. This indicator has been met and exceeded with all new EC equipment installed and tested in January 2025. Regular weekly tests and drills - at a fixed time each week, to be determined by NDMO – should be institutionalized in NDMO with all radio operators across the atolls.

title.narrative: Length of coast with reduced vulnerabilty to flooding and storm surges

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to Subcomponent 2.1.1: Strengthen Coastal Resilience in Ebeye and the coastal protection works in Ebeye. The end target was revised through the second AF, representing existing 300 meter which was deemed not necessary to be rebuilt during the seawall design stage. Seawall contract was signed on May 9, 2024. By end of November 2025, 1421 m seawall has been constructed, out of 1800 m in total.

title.narrative: Number of people who can receive timely and actionable hazard forecast and warning messages

comment.narrative: Achieved. This indicator is linked to the development of the emergency communication (EC) network (equipment installation and associated training) that will transmit the hazard forecasts and warning messages. It is also linked with the related Community Disaster Risk Management Emergency Communication Training (CDRM-ECT) that were completed in all neighboring atolls following the EC Standard Operation Procedure. The Typhoon Preparedness Action Plans and Community Disaster Plans have been developed for eleven Atolls. EC installation was completed by the IOM in January, 2025, completing all 63 stations and covering 100 percent of RMI's population. In addition, 63 communities have been reached, 1369 operators have been trained on basic how to use and how to maintain the EC communication equipment on each atoll, among which 550 are female. Total population in RMI according to the 2021 Census is 42,418, 90 percent of the population is considered beneficiaries.

title.narrative: National Adaptation Plan integrates the results of the coastal vulnerability assessment

comment.narrative: This indicator has been met. This activity is linked to Subcomponent 1.1.1 Institutional strengthening, and central agency capacity building in risk governance. The results of the Coastal Vulnerability Assessment (Deltares 2016 and 2021) have been integrated and streamlined into the National Adaptation Plan (NAP), which has been approved by Cabinet on November 31, 2023 and presented by the GoRMI at the COP28 on December 5, 2023.

title.narrative: NDMO facilities modernized and operating in accordance with key priorities identified in agreed roadmap

comment.narrative: This indicator has been met. This indicator is linked to subcomponent 1.1.3 NDMO facilities. The NDMO Roadmap was finalized in early 2023. The PIU had procured minor items from the NDMO Roadmap including desktop units, tablets, laptops, cell phones, drones, walkie talkies etc. IT and non-IT equipment have been delivered on October 31, 2023; NDMO office has been renovated with ancillary equipment installed on November 15, 2023.

title.narrative: Reduced expected annual damage due to coastal protection interventions

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to Subcomponent 2.1.1: Strengthen Coastal Resilience in Ebeye and the coastal protection works in Ebeye. As detailed in the Coastal Vulnerability Assessment (Deltares, 2016) once the proposed seawall of 2.1 km (including 300 meters existing seawall) is constructed, the reduced expected annual damage was estimated at USD700,000/year. 1421 m of seawall has been constructed, out of 1800 m in total, achieving close to 80 percent of the final target. Therefore, 80 percent of the final target is reported for this ISR. When Seawall construction is close to be completed, the value will be reevaluated.

title.narrative: The Government has developed and adopted procedures to clarify the governance mechanism of the JNAP

comment.narrative: 100 percent achieved. The indicator is linked to Subcomponent 1.1.1 Institutional strengthening, and central agency capacity building in risk governance. A Disaster and Climate Risk Governance Advisor and Disaster Risk Management and Climate Change Adaptation Advisor have worked closely with the CSO, NDMO and other agencies. The following 4 activities have been completed, leading to this indicator being marked as achieved: a) the policy paper governance framework ‘Management of RMI response to climate change and disaster risk – ToR for the Tile TilEo Committee’ is finalized; b) the policy paper Republic of Marshall Islands National Planning Framework is finalized; c) the Structure for Integration & Coordination of Climate Activity is approved by Cabinet, and d) the working groups at national and local government levels are operationalized (the working groups include the Mitigation Working Group and the Adaptation Working Group, the RMI NDC Partnership Working Group).

title.narrative: Time taken to receive funds from contingency emergency component for an eligible emergency.

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to Component 3 - Contingent Emergency Response. CERC training was held in Majuro in October 2018. The CERC Operations Manual has been updated most recently in 2021. The CERC has not been triggered. The project funds allocated to CERC has been reallocated to Component 1 through the second AF. However, this indicator remains per GoRMI's request.

title.narrative: Communities involved in planning/implementation/evaluation of early warning and shoreline protection activities

comment.narrative: This indicator pertains to all communities and stakeholders involved in the planning, implementation and evaluation of early warning activities and shoreline protection activities. Several rounds of stakeholder workshops have been undertaken on design concepts and technical options as well as environmental and social impacts and mitigations related to seawall construction. Consultations have been done well and will continue as needed. The PIU is therefore reporting to have reached the target (Yes) for this indicator.

title.narrative: Number of people with enhanced resilience to climate risks

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to Subcomponent 2.1.1: Strengthen Coastal Resilience in Ebeye and the coastal protection works in Ebeye. 1421 m of seawall has been constructed, out of 1800 m in total, achieving close to 80 percent of the final target.

title.narrative: People with enhanced resilience to climate risks

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to Subcomponent 2.1.1: Strengthen Coastal Resilience in Ebeye and the coastal protection works in Ebeye. Seawall contract was signed on May 9, 2024. As of November 2025, close to 80% of the seawall has been built. Therefore the number of people with enhanced resilience to climate risks in Ebeye is updated to 6500.

title.narrative: Majority of beneficiaries are satisfied with the community consultation of early warning activities

comment.narrative: This indicator pertains to beneficiaries involved in the early warning activities and guided by the Stakeholder Engagement Plan. Relevant activities include the community consultations, design and implementation of the ‘Outer Islands Focal Point Workshop’; the involvement of key stakeholders in the development progress of the Strategic Emergency Communications Roadmap; training of community members on emergency communication equipment and development and implementation of a program of community drills on disaster risk management and emergency communications. The target is met since the majority of the participants (more than 75%) to the national annual focal point training workshop and the ‘Finalization of the Emergency Communication Roadmap’ workshop were satisfied with these consultations based on surveys undertaken after the activities. The current EC network activities will conclude by Jan. 2026, with continued focus on operation, sustainability and capacity building.

title.narrative: Majority of beneficiaries are satisfied with the community consultation on shoreline protection activities

comment.narrative: A survey has been conducted on Ebeye that shows acceptable satisfaction among beneficiaries (more than 75%) and the end target under this indicator is therefore considered met, though there is need for regular and ongoing consultations, in keeping with the project Stakeholder Engagement Plan.

title.narrative: Value of public energy assets protected

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to Subcomponent 2.1.2 Priority coastal protection investments. The value of these assets relates to energy assets intended to be protected in the southern end of Ebeye including the diesel power station and the solar array. The value is still zero since the seawall at the southern end of Ebeye has not been constructed yet. When Seawall construction is close to be completed, the value will be reevaluated.

title.narrative: Development of National Adaptation Plan and adoption by Cabinet

comment.narrative: This indicator has been met. This activity is linked to Subcomponent 1.2.2 Support Disaster and Climate Preparedness, Response, and Adaptation. The Disaster and Climate Risk Governance Adviser, Climate Adaptation Advisor and NAP Coordinator have supported the preparation of the NAP. The NAP has been approved by the Cabinent on November 31, 2023 and presented to the COP on December 5, 2023.
